newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico "cracks down on left" in panic over rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexico "cracks down on left" in panic over rebels.

text.p: Mexico has launched an indiscriminate crackdown on leftists in a desperate bid to find rebels from a new guerrilla group, an opposition front charged on Tuesday.

Leaders of the Broad Front for the Construction of the Movement of National Liberation (FAC-MLN), which includes more than 300 Mexican opposition groups, said the government had threatened, tortured and arrested their members on trumped-up charges. They released a list of 75 "political prisoners" whom they said were wrongfully held.

Many of the prisoners were in solitary confinement in maximum security jails and had no contact with their families, they said. Several had not been tried and had been tortured to confess crimes they had not committed.

"The government is lashing out blindly," said Carlota Botey of the FAC-MLN's National Coordinating Commission. "Since they really have little knowledge of who makes up the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), they are hitting leaders of social organisations."

A previously unknown group, the EPR appeared at the end of June in the state of Guerrero proclaiming a guerrilla struggle against the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. It has since attacked in at least five states, killing more than 20 people, mostly members of the security forces.
Zedillo has vowed to use the full force of the law against the EPR, but government officials deny that human rights have been trampled in the military offensive against the rebels.
The FAC-MLN, which was set up last January and now has branches in 18 states, aims to overthrow the government and topple free-market economic policies via "civil resistance".
FAC-MLN National Coordinating Commission member Benito Moron said his organisation respected "all forms of struggle" against the government's economic policies.
It respects the EPR's armed fight against the government, though it did not share that group's methods because it wanted to stay within the law.
But Cecilia Corona, of the National Assembly of Women, told reporters she was "proud to salute the effort of our comrades from the EPR and I respect their struggle."
The group said it had appealed to Interior Minister Emilio Chuayffet to allow a visit to the political prisoners by a group of government, FAC and human rights representatives.

It cited as especially serious the situation of Porfirio del Angel Contreras, a leader of the Eastern Democratic Front of Mexico arrested without a warrant on Aug. 10 in Mexico City and transferred to a fortress jail in Veracruz state.

"He was submitted to psychological torture ... they are keeping him segregated in solitary confinement in a humid cell plagued with insects, without a bed, blankets or adequate clothing and with insufficient food", the FAC-MLN said.
